# Diagnostics

Use this skill for the Digital Diagnostic, maturity, findings, and diagnostic
logic. The diagnostic is an analysis workspace, not a set of administrative
assessment screens. It should explain the operating environment, assess digital
and operational maturity, identify findings, connect each conclusion to
evidence, and feed opportunities and approved outputs.

Provide a legible maturity profile and let the consultant drill into a
dimension's current state, desired state, gap, evidence, observations,
potential opportunity, and confidence. Keep the active client/site/engagement
context explicit and make incomplete assessment, missing evidence, and the next
useful action visible.

Preserve assessment rationale, evidence links, confidence, assessor/context,
and draft versus approved state. Use an explicit, explainable scoring model;
do not invent arbitrary formulas or generic questionnaires disconnected from
the factory. Make missing evidence and uncertainty visible. Methodology
configuration can remain useful, but belongs in internal configuration rather
than the main diagnostic workflow.

The Digital Landscape Map should be a projection of structured areas, processes,
systems, data, dependencies, people/roles, and observations, not a disconnected
drawing. Keep diagnostic logic testable and separate from presentation. A
Current Understanding synthesis must distinguish evidence-backed facts from
interpretation and assumptions.
